lines.text: There are eight layers between the President of the United States and anyone who wants to hurt him.
The outermost layer is sixty nautical miles wide. The last one is a person.
Layer one. The sky.
Wherever the president goes, the airspace around him closes. A restricted ring, usually thirty nautical miles in every direction.
Inside that sits a second ring, about ten miles out, where almost every flight is banned.
The FAA writes the rules. The military enforces them, with fighter jets.
After the 2025 inauguration, NORAD responded to more than forty planes that wandered into the rings around Mar-a-Lago alone.
Layer two. The advance.
Before the president arrives anywhere, a Secret Service advance team gets there first. For a campaign event, usually three to five days ahead. For a foreign trip, it can be a month.
They walk every place he might go. The hotel, the route, the nearest hospital. Even the bathrooms.
Then the lead agent writes the security plan that every other layer follows.
Layer three. The rooftops.
Outside, a counter sniper team watches from high ground, with long range optics, looking for anyone who should not be there.
And this layer shows what happens when one fails. On July 13, 2024, in Butler, Pennsylvania, a gunman climbed onto a roof about 147 yards from the stage.
That roof had not been secured. Eight shots were fired before a Secret Service counter sniper killed him.
The agency's own review later found failures in its advance planning and in communication with local police.
Layer four. The checkpoint.
Everyone who gets close walks through a magnetometer, run by the Secret Service Uniformed Division. Staff, guests and reporters. No exceptions.
Layer five. The motorcade.
When he moves, local police close the roads, and the president travels inside a convoy that carries its own counter assault team and an ambulance.
The counter assault team has one job. If the motorcade is attacked, they fight, so everyone else can get him out.
Layer six. The Beast.
The president's limousine. Its real specifications are classified, but reports describe doors about eight inches thick, built from steel, aluminum, titanium and ceramic.
Estimates put its weight at around eight tons.
And according to multiple reports, the trunk carries a supply of the president's own blood type, in case he cannot reach a hospital.
Layer seven. The shift.
The agents closest to the president work in rotating shifts, and they talk about him on the radio using a code name.
The Secret Service does not pick those names. They come from a list kept by the White House Communications Agency.
Barack Obama was Renegade. Donald Trump is Mogul. Joe Biden was Celtic.
Layer eight. The last layer.
When every other layer has failed, what is left is an agent's body.
On March 30, 1981, outside the Washington Hilton, shots were fired at Ronald Reagan.
Agent Tim McCarthy turned toward the gunfire and spread his body in front of the president. He was shot in the chest.
He survived. And he was not even supposed to be working that day. He was on the shift because he lost a coin flip.
So that is presidential protection. Sixty nautical miles of closed sky, eight layers of people and steel, and at the very center, sometimes, a coin flip.
Which layer surprised you the most? Tell me in the comments.
